raw:
The text describes the routine work of a night assistant at an observatory. His duties included practical maintenance tasks: he kept the observatory's clock wound and made sure the transit instrument was always ready for use.

One of the observatory's functions was timekeeping for the wider community. Each evening, the exact time determined at the observatory was transmitted over the wire (the telegraph line) to the railway companies. These companies relied on that transmitted time to set the clocks at their stations, meaning the observatory served as the official time source for the railways.

The night assistant also carried out observational and record-keeping work. On clear nights, he recorded several things in his log: the weather conditions, the number of observations that had been made, and the comets he detected. The text notes that the comets he logged were faint ones — objects that could only be found under the right conditions, namely a quiet sky and a patient eye, implying that such discoveries required calm atmospheric conditions and careful, unhurried attention from the observer.
